units.source_text: 古歌：“岩濑森林内，郭公莫乱啼！

en.t: An old poem says: In the forest of Iwase, cuckoo, do not cry out wildly!

units.source_text: 啼时人忆别，相恋更增悲。”

en.t: When you cry, people remember parting, and lovers grow still more sorrowful.

units.source_text: 又：“君若恋我时，来见岂不好。

en.t: Another says: If you long for me, would it not be better to come and see me?

units.source_text: 何必托人传言语，犹似岩濑林中郭公鸟！”

en.t: Why entrust your words to someone else, like the cuckoo in the woods of Iwase?

units.source_text: 但此处引用此二歌，皆不恰当。

en.t: But quoting these two poems here is inappropriate in both cases.

units.source_text: 据《湖月抄》说：“岩濑”（地名）与“托人传言”发音相同。

en.t: According to Kogetsusho, Iwase, a place name, is pronounced the same as entrusting a message to someone.

units.source_text: 此处引用此句，是不托人传言而对面共话之意。

en.t: The line is quoted here to mean speaking face to face together, without asking someone else to carry a message.
